PullRequest.Title: Browser tools: dialog flake in the click and typing tools test (#350285)
PullRequest.Body:
Work in progress for #350285. `chat - browser tools › click and typing tools can handle dialogs in main, opaque, and nested frames` still fails in the merge queue after #350301.

Right now this branch only holds a temporary commit. It loops the whole `chat - browser tools` suite 40 times in CI, so each round starts from the state the previous tests leave behind, and adds diagnostics to the failing assertion. That commit gets dropped before this PR is ready. It will become either the fix or a skip that links the issue.

> Authored with Copilot

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The complete test file establishes the case counts, and testrunner.js loads all test files into a non-parallel Mocha runner. The awaited tool calls cross extension-host RPC, browser creation/navigation, and shared-process Playwright IPC. Session caching reduces initialization, not repeated test execution. Actual elapsed time and timeout incidence are unmeasured.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Sequential browser-view creation/navigation, extension-host and shared-process IPC calls, Playwright/CDP actions, and configuration-file edits.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Test-case and hook execution counts grow exactly 40-fold for matching desktop cases (12 to 480 locally; 10 to 400 remotely). Browser work remains serial across rounds; cached Playwright session initialization is not multiplied by 40, but forceNew page creation and individual actions are.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Longer integration-test feedback and CI critical-path latency, with increased risk of exhausting the existing step timeout.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The suite was registered once: 12 local desktop cases or 10 remote desktop cases, with one setup/teardown and one sequence of tool/browser operations per case.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every ordinary desktop single-folder integration run now executes all browser-tool cases and their setup/teardown 40 times sequentially: 480 cases locally, or 400 with a remote extension host, instead of 12 or 10.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 23 wraps the entire existing suite in `for (let round = 0; round < 40; round++)`, replacing the single suite registration with 40 distinct registrations. The loop is unconditional for desktop runs; it is not gated on CI or a diagnostic environment variable.
Findings.Title: Make the 40-round browser stress run opt-in
Findings.Impact: Running the normal desktop API integration suite, or reproducing one test with --grep, now includes 39 extra executions of each matching browser test. This adds sequential browser navigation, dialog automation, RPC, and settings-edit latency to developer feedback and CI completion, increasing pressure on the existing 15-minute CI budget.
Findings.Evidence: test/integration/electron/testrunner.js:26-46 applies only an optional MOCHA_GREP and otherwise runs every loaded test serially. scripts/test-integration.sh:286-287 includes this file through the singlefolder-tests directory; .github/workflows/pr-linux-test.yml:539-548 runs it under a 15-minute extension-host step. Each case performs awaited configuration updates and editor cleanup (changed file:28-58). Tool invocations use extHostLanguageModelTools.ts:124 RPC; OpenBrowserTool._openNewPage creates a browser view and awaits navigation/readiness, while Playwright calls use the shared-process proxy. Multiple cases explicitly set forceNew, so warm session/page caches cannot remove the repeated browser work.
Findings.Recommendation: Make the 40-round stress reproduction explicitly opt-in, with one round by default, or remove the temporary repetition before merging. Keep diagnostics independent of the repetition gate.

Scenarios.Scenario: Normal local desktop single-folder API integration run, including CI and grep-filtered developer runs
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The Mocha runner must finish every matching browser test, including awaited setup, tool operations, navigation/readiness, and teardown, before the API suite completes. The diff expands the browser portion from 12 to 480 executable cases. CI has an existing 15-minute extension-host step budget.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Launch the Electron application with the singlefolder-tests extension entry point.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing Electron suite launch per API-folder run, not one launch per round.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same launch executed one browser-tools suite registration; now it executes 40. No new shell subprocess call was added.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The invoking test script waits for application/test completion, so extra in-process test work delays this existing boundary's completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send each lm.invokeTool request to the workbench through $invokeTool and return the serialized result.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One RPC per issued tool invocation, multiplied across 40 executions of each matching test; no batching or tool-result cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical tool operations were issued for one round. The diff multiplies their execution frequency by 40.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Tests await each invocation before their next dependent action.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create/resolve native browser views and await loadURL and page readiness.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Eight forceNew tool opens per full local round, now 320 instead of eight; five additional direct openBrowserTab calls per storage test, now 200 instead of five. Three other tool opens per round may reuse an eligible existing page.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One round of those operations. The diff increases their frequency, not the underlying browser-view API.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Browser creation, navigation, and summary readiness block their test's next step.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Forward Playwright operations to the shared process and issue CDP traffic to browser views.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Individual actions and summaries are repeated across 40 rounds. CDP session initialization is cached by <default> and coalesced while pending; this is not 40 independent Playwright browser connections.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One round of actions on the same cached-session architecture.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited dialog, typing, click, evaluation, and summary operations are on the test completion path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Update global settings through configuration RPC, queued JSON model edits, and text-file saves when changed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Four setup/teardown configuration-update requests per test: 48 to 1,920 for the full local browser suite, plus storage-test-specific updates. Actual saves exclude no-op edits.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same per-test settings changes occurred for 12 cases once, not 480 cases.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Setup, teardown, and storage-test configuration updates are awaited; configuration editing serializes writes through a Queue.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create local HTTP fixture servers and navigate browser pages, load child frames, and make probe/release requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Six server lifecycles per full local round become 240; the associated page/frame/probe requests recur each round. New ephemeral ports and forceNew pages prevent a warm page cache from eliminating the fixture workflows.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Six fixture-server lifecycles and one execution of their network workflows.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Page readiness, frame removal, and storage assertions wait for corresponding network activity; finally blocks close connections/servers before proceeding.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load the test workspace index.html via file:// and exercise its worker-backed interaction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One workflow becomes 40 workflows; OS caching can reduce physical reads but not the repeated browser/worker actions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The case waits for page readiness and worker response before reading the page.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: 40 registrations of 12 local desktop test cases; with grep, each matching case still runs 40 times. Within the dialog case, five fixed frame prefixes remain unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Mocha is configured without parallel mode and executes these suites/tests sequentially. Awaited actions within cases are largely serial. Notification clearing runs every 500 ms during each test; storage-test tab closure uses Promise.all over a small bounded set. Linux runs separate extension suites with INTEGRATION_TEST_PARALLEL=2, which does not parallelize these 40 rounds.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Tool registration and module loading can be warm after the first round. All calls without an invocation context use the same <default> Playwright session; existing sessions and in-flight initialization are reused/deduplicated. There is no result cache for individual tool actions. forceNew bypasses existing-page reuse; teardown closes editors, and setup/teardown repeatedly changes configuration. Settings saves occur when edits actually change the model, not on every possible no-op.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the unconditional changed loop, full case inventory, serial runner, normal CI inclusion, RPC implementation, browser readiness path, and session caching were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No elapsed-time measurements were collected; exact added duration and incidence of exhausting the CI timeout depend on host speed and test behavior. Operation and case multiplicity are directly established.
Scenarios.Verdict: One medium-severity repeated-work finding submitted at added line 23: make stress repetition opt-in instead of multiplying every ordinary desktop run.

Scenarios.Scenario: Desktop UI with a remote extension host running the browser API suite
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The API suite waits for 400 browser cases instead of 10, including remote extension-host RPC, browser readiness, and remote-hosted HTTP fixtures.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send remote extension-host tool requests to the desktop workbench.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: The existing invocation sequence for each of 10 remote-enabled cases is executed 40 times, rather than once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One execution of each remote-enabled case's invocation sequence.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited round trips precede each dependent browser action and assertion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create browser views and run shared-process Playwright/CDP operations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Seven forceNew tool opens per remote round become 280 instead of seven, plus two non-forceNew opens per round subject to reuse. Session connection setup is shared, not per item.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same work for one round; the diff increases frequency only.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Navigation readiness and automation results block each case.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reach HTTP fixtures served from the remote extension host through the browser's existing remote proxy or applicable forwarded-localhost handling.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Five fixture-server lifecycles per remote round become 200, with recurring top-level, child-frame, and release requests. Exact proxy connection count depends on existing transport reuse.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One round of the same remote-fixture workflows.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Tests await navigations, frame removal, and summaries before continuing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Apply the global setup/teardown settings edits using the existing configuration write queue and save changed models.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Four configuration requests per executable case: 40 before versus 1,600 after. Actual saves are conditional on edits; the remote-skipped storage case adds none.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same global configuration workflow for 10 cases once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Setup and teardown await updates and serialized configuration writes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: 10 remote-enabled desktop cases multiplied by 40; storage isolation and file:// cases are skipped.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The same serial Mocha execution and awaited actions apply. The 40 rounds do not create 40 parallel test workers. Remote network transport may add latency to each existing awaited action.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The storage and file-backed interaction cases are explicitly skipped remotely. The shared <default> Playwright session remains cached/coalesced. Seven forceNew opens per round remain uncached page creations; non-forceNew opens can reuse eligible pages. No tool-action result cache removes repeated RPC.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: explicit remote skip guards, runner ordering, tool RPC, remote-localhost handling, and cached Playwright session ownership were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Remote transport latency and how frequently remote integration runs execute were not measured. The increased serial operation count is certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Same root cause as the submitted loop finding, not a separate issue.

Scenarios.Scenario: Collect diagnostics when the click/dialog assertion fails
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A missing alert now waits three seconds, invokes diagnostic Playwright code, and then fails. This delays that test's failure reporting; the successful path does not enter the diagnostic branch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke run_playwright_code through extension-host and shared-process RPC to evaluate active elements.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one added diagnostic invocation per failed execution of the dialog test; at most 40 if all repeated executions fail. The DOM scan covers the fixed four top-level iframe elements.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The assertion failed immediately without the timer or additional evaluation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Failure reporting awaits the three-second timer and the invocation, which uses the existing default five-second tool execution timeout.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Return and format a small object containing active-element IDs and four frame diagnostic strings.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One bounded diagnostic payload per failed test execution; no collection or history accumulation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only the original click result was included in the failed assertion.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The payload is included in the assertion failure after the tool finishes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: First failing prefix out of five fixed prefixes per test execution; four top-level fixture iframes in the diagnostic evaluation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One awaited timer followed by one awaited tool invocation. assert.fail stops the frame loop on its first failing prefix, so diagnostics are not issued for all five prefixes in one case.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Diagnostics target the already-open page and reuse the existing Playwright session. There is no retry loop or new page creation in this branch.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: branch condition, single invocation, fixed fixture DOM, default timeout, and immediate assertion abort are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Failure frequency is unknown. The explicit added three-second delay is known, but total diagnostic invocation duration is not measured.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: this is bounded failure-only diagnostic work, not successful-path overhead or unbounded scanning. Repetition-related amplification is covered by the loop finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Web integration runs and normal application browser-tool use
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Web UI chooses suite.skip, so browser test hooks and tool calls do not execute. Normal application use does not load this test file.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: 480 registered skipped cases in a web test process; no user-page-dependent scale and no production-path multiplicity change.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No browser-test runtime work on the web-skipped path; only 40 bounded suite/test registrations occur. Application runtime scheduling is unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No browser or Playwright session is initialized by skipped cases. Production cache behavior is unchanged because no production implementation changed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the suite.skip UIKind guard and test-only changed-file inventory establish path exclusion.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Skipped-test metadata/reporting overhead was not measured and is too small and bounded here to support an independent finding.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable web or production-runtime regression; the submitted finding is limited to desktop integration-test execution.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over the complete one-file inventory and all three diff hunks against base eed628b4b515f6483baed1c58fd13573ae679f98. Submitted one high-confidence medium-severity regression for unconditional 40-fold serial browser-test repetition. Bounded failure diagnostics, web skips, session caching, fixture cleanup, and local/remote boundaries were considered. No concrete removed performance regression warranted blame/fix reporting. Static read-only review; elapsed durations remain unmeasured.
